text:
wen: hi team, wen here  first day. building the runtime + a cuda plugin and the binary fails to load with an undefined symbol at runtime. any quick ideas?

wen: build command: `cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo && cmake --build build -j12`

wen: runtime error when loading plugin:
```
/usr/bin/python: symbol lookup error: /home/wen/repo/build/lib/libcuda_plugin.so: undefined symbol: __cudaRegisterFatBinary
```

wen: host: Ubuntu 22.04 WSL2 with Docker Desktop GPU passthrough. CUDA toolkit installed at /usr/local/cuda-12.2. I built the plugin with nvcc compilation + clang for host objects.

alex: welcome! :wave: that symbol is emitted by cudart when static fatbinary registration is used. usually indicates the plugin wasn't linked against cudart or the object files were compiled with incompatible PIC/link flags. what does `ldd build/lib/libcuda_plugin.so` show?

wen: `ldd build/lib/libcuda_plugin.so` shows it links to `libcudart.so.12 => /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so.12` and others. i expected that to satisfy the symbol.
rishi: two common cases: 1) the plugin contains device-side fatbin sections that expect the host binary to include cudart static registration helper (linker ordering can drop it), or 2) you compiled CUDA objects with `-c` producing `*.o` that contain cuda registration but the final shared lib link used `--as-needed` and dropped the static cudart dependency. Did you compile device objs with `-dc`/`-dlink`?

wen: i compiled `nvcc -arch=sm_86 -c src/kernel.cu -o kernel.o` and then `clang++ -shared -o libcuda_plugin.so kernel.o plugin_wrapper.o -L${CUDA_HOME}/lib64 -lcudart`.
gabi: try compiling the cuda objects with `nvcc -dc` (relocatable device code) and then link with `nvcc -dlink` before final link so the device symbols are resolved into a device linking object. Alternatively, link against cudart_static with proper whole-archive flags. Also ensure `-fPIC` for host objects. Example flow: `nvcc -dc -Xcompiler -fPIC kernel.cu -o kernel.o` then `nvcc -dlink kernel.o -o device_link.o` then `clang++ -shared -fPIC plugin_wrapper.o kernel.o device_link.o -Wl,--no-as-needed -lcudart`

rishi: and if you're using CMake, set `CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION=ON` (or add `-dc` into CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS) and set `CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON`. Also avoid `--as-needed` on the linker by setting `CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS` to include `-Wl,--no-as-needed` for the plugin target.

wen: thanks — i rebuilt with `nvcc -dc -Xcompiler -fPIC` and added `device_link.o` from `-dlink`. also set `-Wl,--no-as-needed` and explicitly added `-lcudart` late in the link line. plugin now loads without symbol error. :tada:

alex: nice! could you drop a short note in the repo README about building shared cuda plugins (nvcc -dc / -dlink and PIC) so future new hires hit this less? we had one PR months ago but it was terse.

build-bot: build passed for commit 04b2a on linux-x86_64. tests: gpu smoke ok.

onboard-bot: Welcome wen! Please complete the "Runtime dev setup" checklist in Notion and add your working host/toolkit combo to the onboarding doc.

wen: will add a small HOWTO to docs and the onboarding doc. thanks everyone!
_description: Onboarding thread: new hire hits undefined symbol __cudaRegisterFatBinary when loading a CUDA plugin shared library. Team diagnoses missing device-link step and PIC flags (nvcc -dc / -dlink), linker ordering (--no-as-needed), and suggests CMake flags and README update.
